course_info.trial_description:
Hello! I'm glad to see that you're interested in learning English! As a native English speaker, I can assure you that it's a valuable skill to have, no matter what your future goals may be.

For your trial lesson, we'll start by introducing some basic vocabulary and grammar rules. We'll also work on some pronunciation exercises to help you develop your language skills. Don't worry if you make mistakes - learning a new language takes time and practice!

Throughout the lesson, I'll provide plenty of opportunities for you to ask questions and practice your new skills. By the end of the session, you'll have a better understanding of English and be ready to continue your language learning journey.

I'm excited to work with you and help you achieve your language goals. Let's get started!

pro_course_detail.title: Conversational Practise (Free talk)
pro_course_detail.description:
Welcome to the conversational practice lesson plan for all English levels. We'll be focusing on improving your speaking skills and fluency in English through various activities.

First, we'll start with a warm-up activity where we will have an icebreaker. This is a great way to get comfortable with speaking and to practice your listening skills.

Next, we'll move on to a role-playing activity where you'll have the chance to practice real-life scenarios such as ordering food in a restaurant or booking a hotel room. This activity will help you develop your confidence and ability to communicate effectively in English.

After that, we'll do a 1-1 discussion where you'll be given a topic to discuss with me. This will give you the opportunity to express your opinions and ideas while also learning from others.

Finally, we'll end the lesson with a feedback session where you'll receive constructive feedback from your teacher on your speaking skills and how you can improve.

Remember, the key to improving your speaking skills is to practice as much as possible. So, don't be afraid to make mistakes, and keep practicing until you feel confident and comfortable speaking in English. Good luck!

pro_course_detail.title: General Lesson (Pronunciation, Grammar, Listening)
pro_course_detail.description:
Welcome to my general lesson plan that covers pronunciation, grammar, and listening for all levels. In this lesson, we will focus on improving your overall communication skills in English. We'll start with pronunciation, which is crucial for making yourself understood. We'll go over some common vowel and consonant sounds that non-native speakers might struggle with and practice pronouncing them correctly. 

Next, we'll move on to grammar, which is the backbone of any language. We'll review some of the most important grammar rules, such as verb tenses, articles, prepositions, and sentence structure. We'll also do some exercises to reinforce what we've learned and help you make fewer mistakes when you speak or write in English.

Finally, we'll work on your listening skills, which are essential for understanding what others are saying. We'll listen to different types of audio, such as recordings of conversations, news reports, or podcasts, and practice listening for specific information. We'll also discuss some common English idioms and expressions that might be difficult to understand at first.

By the end of this lesson, you'll have improved your pronunciation, grammar, and listening skills, and you'll be one step closer to speaking English fluently and confidently. let's get started!

pro_course_detail.title: Accents, Pronunciation, and Spelling
pro_course_detail.description:
Did you know that there are 44 sounds (known as phonemes) in the English language? There are also a number of pronunciation differences between American English, British English, and English spoken in specific countries.

If you really want to focus on being better understood in English, to sound more fluent, to improve your spelling, and to improve your listening skills in English, then this is the class for you! 

In this class the following areas will be covered:

-Pronunciation, accent, and word differences that you are likely to hear in New Zealand, Australia, Britain and the USA. 

-Word stress and syllables
Sometimes when we learn a new language, it can be hard to hear what syllable or letter we need to emphasise in a word, or sentence. When we emphasise the wrong part of a word, or sentence, it can completely change the way a word / sentence sounds.

-Mouth Shape / Tongue Placement
Often we don't think about, or know where our tongue needs to be, in relation to different parts of the mouth. This is quite important for achieving particular sounds in any language. For example the 'th' sound in English requires the tongue to pass between our front teeth for a brief moment. This part of the lesson will cover techniques to help you to achieve those difficult sounds that you may not have in your own native language.

-Spelling in English
 Words are not written as they sound in English. This part of the class focuses on how to recognise words in their written form, and how to match the sounds with the spelling. For example, some of the words that we will discuss in this class are: through, though, thought, words with silent letters, such as: knight, night, knife, island, and words ending in the letter, 'y', such as: sky, fly, buy, etc....

I look forward to helping you improve in these specific areas.

Book your lesson today!

pro_course_detail.title: IELTS Preparation
pro_course_detail.description:
These lessons are designed to assist you as you prepare for your IELTS examination.

You will have the opportunity to practise the individual skills that you need the most help with, (reading, writing, listening, or speaking) in each lesson. There will be question and answer time during each lesson.

PACKAGED LESSON STRUCTURE

*Lesson 1_IELTS Introduction / Overview
General Training vs Academic; band score and marking criteria; create a study action plan; test format; question formats; areas of concern.

-Lesson 2_SPEAKING
*Understanding the IELTS Speaking question formats; marking criteria; practice tests; interesting vocabulary worksheets; how to sound more fluent; tips to help overcome the fear of making mistakes when speaking; pronunciation; error feedback; questions and concerns.

-Lesson 3_LISTENING
*Understanding the IELTS Listening question formats; marking criteria; practice tests; discussing the sub skills of listening (prediction, listening for gist vs listening for detail); sounds; error feedback; questions and concerns.

-Lesson 4_READING 
*Understanding the IELTS Reading question formats; marking criteria; practice tests; discussing the sub skills of reading (prediction, reading for gist vs reading for detail); new vocabulary meaning, form, and pronunciation; error feedback; questions and concerns.

-Lesson 5_WRITING Overview
*Understanding the IELTS Writing question formats; marking criteria; practice tests; simple, compound, and complex sentences; writing structures; how to organise your ideas logically; punctuation, spelling tips, error feedback; questions and concerns.

-Lesson 6_WRITING: ESSAYS & LETTERS
*Understanding your audience;  informal vs formal; correct collocation of interesting vocabulary; how to start and finish well; logical flow of ideas.

*Lessons 7-10_SPECIFIC SKILLS
-These lessons will be tailored to your specific needs: reading, writing, speaking, or listening. They will also cover exam time management.

teacher_info.about_teacher: I have a passion for teaching. The great thing about teaching is, you can shape young minds and help them to achieve their full potential. I believe that classes should be fun because if it is boring the students will not remember the lessons and they will not want to learn anymore. Even though I try to make the classes fun, I still push my students to achieve their potential because at the end of the day, they need to be able to use what they have learned.
teacher_info.teaching_style: My teaching style is one where I just help and guide the students to the right path rather than having them repeat after me like a parrot. Depending on their level, we will start off with flash cards and objects to improve their vocabulary. As they progress will make short sentences and then from there we will try to have a conversation where I can help them with their grammar and pronunciation. If I do give homework it will be something they can learn and use in their every day life, for example I will tell them to choose a dish they like making and then to write a recipe in English or Afrikaans so that they can tell me how to make it. I want the students to do most of the talking.
